hero.kicker: TWO DAYS TO THE FINAL · SPAIN–ARGENTINA
hero.headline: THE STREAK MEETS THE DYNASTY.
hero.standfirst: No football today — just the numbers gathering weight. Spain bring a 37-match unbeaten run across all competitions and the stingiest defence in World Cup history. Argentina bring a 13-game unbeaten World Cup streak, a 39-year-old rewriting endings, and the chance to become the first back-to-back champions since Brazil in 1962. Two days. One trophy. And before it, a Golden Boot playoff in Miami.
hero.photoCaption: Lamine Yamal — managing a hamstring, carrying Spain's right flank, two days from the biggest game of his life

briefing.text: Team news: Yamal has been managing hamstring trouble but remains central to everything Spain do. Argentina came through Atlanta without a fresh injury concern.
The Boot: Messi's two Atlanta assists bolster his tie-break, but Mbappé strikes first — Saturday against England, one goal for the outright lead.
The Crystal Ball returns tomorrow with the third-place call, then Sunday morning with the big one. Record so far: 5 winners from 9, two exact scores.

today.preview: The bronze nobody craves, the Boot everybody watches. Mbappé and Dembélé get one more night to add to 8 and 5; Kane (5) and Bellingham (4) get one last England shift of the summer. The market has hardened French: 51% against 25 for England, with 26 on the draw — England's response to Atlanta, four days on, is the great unknown. The Crystal Ball makes its third-place call tomorrow morning.

keyMan.line: Five goals, one game left in an England shirt this summer. A hat-trick in Miami would tie the leaders — unlikely, but this is the fixture where strange things happen.

today.preview: Thirty-seven games unbeaten against thirteen World Cup games unbeaten — something breaks Sunday. Spain have conceded twice all tournament and suffocated France; Argentina have spent three straight knockouts proving no lead against them is safe. Yamal, nursing that hamstring, against Messi, nursing history. The money keeps drifting Spanish: 43 to 27 with 32 on the draw, and over a million dollars down.
